coreRequests.want: core/render.js: set renderer.shadowMap.type explicitly to THREE.PCFShadowMap (or accept the substitution knowingly)
coreRequests.why: three r185 deprecates PCFSoftShadowMap and silently swaps in PCFShadowMap with a console warning. The substitution is not cosmetic: PCFShadowMap is the only branch of WebGLShadowMap that sets compareFunction on shadow.map.depthTexture, so the shadow map is a COMPARE_REF_TO_TEXTURE sampler and any module reading it must declare sampler2DShadow. Reading it as sampler2D drops the draw call silently - no console error, the draw still counted. environment lost most of a round to this. Naming the type in core makes the contract visible.

coreRequests.want: core/render.js: create the WebGLRenderer with stencil: true
coreRequests.why: Overlapping projected sprite shadows multiply (dst*shade twice) and the exact fix is one-fragment-per-pixel, which needs a stencil test. Without it the only idempotent option is depth-write from the shadow plane, and that occludes every transparent pass drawn after it (measured: it ate unrelated scene elements in a full-frame A/B). The compounding is small now that the shadows are the caster's own height, so this is a quality request, not a blocker. Cost is one stencil attachment on the main target.

coreRequests.want: the cave preset's ambient/exposure lifted so unlit rock is dark rather than (0,0,0), OR a way for a biome to register a wide, weak fill light that is not subject to environment/lamps.js's POOL_REACH 3.9 clamp
coreRequests.why: cave/pool is 12.43% and cave/close 16.23% of pixels at exactly (0,0,0), against docs/refs/02 at 0.00% and 04 at 0.06%. It is NOT shadows: --envNoShadow 1 on --showcase hunts --mode cave --preset close --tod 12 is BYTE-IDENTICAL to the control, max channel delta 0 over 1,440,000 px (docs/progress/hunts/r4/ab/cave-close-12-noshadow.png vs -on.png), which also means round 3's open issue 'sun shadows are still cast inside the sealed cave' is wrong as written. And it is no longer albedo: hunts lifted the cold rock tint from 0x1f2740 to 0x6c7691 this round and the pool frame only came from 27.29% to 12.43%, because instanceColor multiplies and a near-black bw2-cave set3 texel stays near black however white the tint. hunts owns lamp placement and has eleven bulbs down there, but lamps.js clamps every PointLight's reach to POOL_REACH 3.9 world units whatever radius is asked for, so a biome physically cannot fill a 56x54 room with placed light. This is the last thing between the cave and ref02's 0.194 mean saturation / 254 p99.  Related and NOT a re-file: coreRequests #27 and #35 already ask for a less saturated, less warm cave preset (the fog is 0x4a2f18 at density 0.040 with `saturation: 1.30`), and this round moved mean saturation on the default framing from a round-2 control's 0.588 to 0.516 without touching any of that — so #35 still stands and is still the larger term. This request is only about the *black*: 12-16% of the frame at exactly (0,0,0) against references at 0.00% and 0.06%.

coreRequests.want: A shadow that fades with distance from its caster, in core/render.js - either a second depth channel carrying the caster distance, or a cheap approximation such as attenuating the shadow term by the receiver depth minus the shadow-map depth.
coreRequests.why: The oldest open visual defect in the project (four rounds) is caster-less slabs at low sun. Round 6 isolated it: they are real, correctly alpha-tested tree shadows from casters standing outside the frame, raked 6.6x by an 8.64-degree shown sun at tod 17.5 and 16.6x at 18:00 (?envCasterOff=tree,pine removes 100% of them). Fading a shadow with distance from its caster keeps the short contact shadow that reads and drops the 25-unit ribbon that does not, and it is the one lever a preset cannot reach.

coreRequests.want: Either document that colour-valued grade uniforms (lift/gain) are converted sRGB->linear by THREE.Color, or add a display-space colour helper to core/config.js.
coreRequests.why: DECISIONS #50(a): presets.js authors lift as a display-space hex because that is what a post-tonemap offset is, but new THREE.Color(hex) with ColorManagement on delivers it in linear - 0x191c28 arrives as (2.5,3.0,5.4)/255, not (25,28,40). Two rounds raised the night lift against contrast's crush point using the hex bytes and moved nothing, and the frames measured 4.6-8.4% of pixels at exactly rgb(0,0,0). This is a trap any module writing a colour uniform can fall into.

integratorFindings.topic: coast: the shoreline staircase with no surf (hunts' open issue #8)
integratorFindings.verdict: CONFIRMED, still present after the round-2 fix, and the cause is now pinned. Cropped the deep/shallow boundary at 2x: long axis-aligned runs meeting at right angles with no transition tile of any kind, while the sand/grass boundary one band below it scallops correctly because it is autotiled.
integratorFindings.cause: `deep = water.clone().shrink(3)` is an erosion, and eroding by 3 removes every one-cell feature, so the deep-water region is a SMOOTHED copy of the coastline — which quantised onto the grid is a clean staircase. The deep region is then laid as flat cells with no border family, so its edge is blocky whatever shape it has.
integratorFindings.triedAndReverted: fraying the deep edge after the erosion (ragged 0.5 / period 3, despeckle 4). It makes it worse: without border tiles, every frayed cell is another hard rectangle, so the edge goes from a straight staircase to floating dark-blue blocks. Looked at it, reverted it.
integratorFindings.theActualFix: bw2-adastra ships a complete 13-slot `walk_edge` family — corners, edges and inner corners — tagged `foam` and `surf`, and it is not being used on this boundary at all. The model named `sea` has no border family, so the deep water can only ever be blocky on its own; the foam belongs to the shallows and should ring the wadeable region on BOTH its edges, against the land and against the deep. That is hunts/biomes/coast.js's to make.

integratorFindings.topic: the mirrored set0 transition slots (hunts' coreRequest: 'the V-convention belongs in the exporter')
integratorFindings.verdict: THE MIRROR IS REAL and I confirmed it independently of hunts: for grass_path_side_edge_w the vertex at world (0,0) — the WEST corner — carries u=0.0 and the east corner u=1.0, so U runs backwards against world X. The cause is the same one DECISIONS #5 records for winding: converting PDSMS's Z-up/Y-south space swaps two axes, which is a mirror, and the winding was realigned for it while the texture coordinates were not. Almost nothing shows it because ground, cliff and water art is tiling or near-symmetric; the transition slots are neither.
integratorFindings.triedAndReverted: flipping U in tools/assets/pdsts.js and rebuilding all 13 packs. The regression gate came back 1 improved / 0 regressed — but the gate measures histograms, not layout, so I scanned the road directly. The green ribbon splitting the path went from 6px to 16px: WORSE. hunts already ships a compensating 180-degree rotation on those two slots (SET0_OUTWARD in src/hunts/palette.js), so fixing the exporter double-corrects them.
integratorFindings.theActualFix: exporter and workaround must move together, in one change: flip U in pdsts.js, rebuild every pack, and delete SET0_OUTWARD in the same commit. Worth doing because the workaround cannot reach the four outer and four inner corner slots — their art is diagonal, and a quarter turn moves it to the wrong diagonal — which is why the road still breaks at every meander step. That is a coordinated tools+hunts change and belongs in one commissioned round, not in an integrator patch to one half of it.
integratorFindings.alsoLearned: the gate has a blind spot worth naming: it reduces frames to luminance and saturation histograms, so it catches brightness, crush and performance regressions and is silent on composition. A layout defect still needs a scanline or an eye.
integratorFindings.secondAttempt: Tried the coordinated version too — flip U in the exporter AND delete SET0_OUTWARD in the same change, which was my own prescription. Road scanline at y=700, interior green gaps: workaround only [6px], exporter only [16px], BOTH [16px, 15px]. The coordinated fix is the worst of the three. So the U mirror is real but it is NOT what causes the ribbons, and my prescription was wrong. Both halves reverted; the shipped state (workaround only, 6px) is the best of the three.
integratorFindings.whatIsActuallyLeft: hunts' own critic already had this right and I should have believed it: 'SET0_OUTWARD turns edge_w/edge_e only; the corner cases are deliberately left mirrored, so each step stamps a green grass comma INSIDE the tan.' The residual gaps are at MEANDER STEPS — the eight corner slots — whose art is diagonal, so neither a 180-degree turn nor a U flip can place it correctly. That needs per-slot handling, not a global convention change.
